requirement.title: Launcher read-projection provenance truthfulness
requirement.body: ADV maintains a durable, launcher-consumable active-state disk projection (`active-launcher-state.json` under the per-project external-state dir) that aggregates active changes from the existing per-change `{changeId}.json` projections. The projection MUST: (a) list only draft/non-terminal changes; (b) exclude archived/terminal changes per `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`, matched by canonical `change.json.id` (NOT archive directory name); (c) carry truthful provenance at all times — `source:"disk_projection"`, `schema_version`, `generated_at`, a last-mutation `freshness` timestamp, an advisory `degraded` flag, and `epics_available:false` (active epics remain Temporal-only and are NEVER fabricated as live). The aggregate is regenerated eagerly after every change mutation as host-side filesystem I/O (Temporal is NOT in the aggregate-write path); a producer-owned rebuild trigger regenerates it from the on-disk per-change set for drift recovery. The aggregate is written by extending the body of the existing `writeChangeProjection` activity (host-side) — NOT by adding a new activity invocation to the workflow — so in-flight workflow histories replay identically (no `wf.patch`/versioning required). The aggregate write is best-effort: a failure must not fail the per-change projection write or the signal.

# Add ADV Launcher Read Projection

## Cross-Project Origin

- **Source project:** toolbox (`/home/jon/toolbox`)
- **Source change:** `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` (consumer-side: zlauncher reads the projection this change produces)
- **Relationship:** producer side of the producer/consumer read-model split approved in `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal`'s discovery + design.
- **Linked at:** 2026-07-23T15:20:53Z; target project = advance (`bdf259aa162ae192af5b18899ccdc653b085528d`).

## Why

`decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` (toolbox) makes zlauncher read a durable, producer-owned disk projection (`active-launcher-state.json`) instead of the Temporal-hard `adv status` CLI, so ADV changes stay visible when Temporal is unavailable. **This change produces that projection** in the advance plugin/store layer. It owns the producer-side acceptance criteria AC1/SC1/SC3 from the parent agreement; the consumer change owns AC2/AC3/AC4/SC2/SC4.

Root defect this resolves: the standalone `adv status` / `adv epic list` CLI is Temporal-hard (no disk-fallback), while the MCP `adv_change_list` layer has disk-fallback — so the launcher silently vanished on any Temporal outage while agents kept working. Rather than patch the intentionally Bun-safe/storage-free CLI boundary (`bin/lib/cli-source-boundary.test.ts`), the validated direction is a producer-owned aggregate read-projection consumed by file.

## User Outcomes

- A launcher (or any consumer) can show ADV's active changes without depending on Temporal being reachable — the display survives Temporal outages.
- Consumers read a single, stable, versioned file instead of shelling out to a Temporal-live CLI.
- Provenance is truthful at all times: the consumer always knows whether it is reading a disk projection or live data, and how fresh it is.
- No regression for existing `adv status` / `adv epic list` users — those stay Temporal-live probes.

## What Changes

1. **Aggregate projection writer** — combine the existing per-change `{changeId}.json` projections into `active-launcher-state.json` under the per-project external-state dir.
2. **Write lifecycle** — regenerate after the existing per-change projection write, and on create / disk-first-close / archive, plus a producer-owned rebuild trigger.
3. **Truthful provenance** — `schema_version`, `generated_at`, `source:"disk_projection"`, `freshness` (last-mutation timestamp), `degraded`, `epics_available:false` (active epics remain Temporal-only; never fabricated as live).
4. **Atomic write** (reuse `atomicWriteFile`: temp + rename + sync) with bounded active-change summaries.
5. **Producer-owned rebuild/repair trigger** — MCP tool / plugin-internal, regenerate from the on-disk per-change projection set for drift recovery. NOT a `bin/adv` subcommand (CLI source-boundary guard).

## Scope

### In Scope
- Aggregate `active-launcher-state.json` projection writer (producer side).
- Write lifecycle hooks on change mutations (create / persist / close / archive) + rebuild trigger.
- Truthful provenance fields + versioned schema.
- Atomic write + bounded summaries.

### Out of Scope
- Active-epic offline projection (further follow-up; epics remain Temporal-required).
- zlauncher consumer changes (owned by `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` in toolbox).
- Removing Temporal from ADV (Temporal stays system of record).
- Changing the standalone `adv status` / `adv epic list` CLI read path (stays Temporal-live).

### Must Not
- **Must not** make `bin/adv` reach `plugin/src/storage` — keep `bin/lib/cli-source-boundary.test.ts` green.
- **Must not** emit `source:"temporal", live:true` (or any live-claiming provenance) for projection data (P33).
- **Must not** fabricate active-epic data as live — `epics_available` must be truthful.
- **Must not** include terminal/archived changes in the active projection — respect `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01` (archive bundle dominates stale non-terminal shadows).
- **Must not** break existing `adv status` / `adv epic list` consumers (additive only).
- **Must not** introduce a non-atomic write (a partial/truncated projection must never be observable).

## Acceptance Criteria (owned here — inherited from parent agreement)

- **AC1** — ADV maintains a durable, launcher-consumable active-state projection on disk, written on change mutations (create/persist/close/archive) with a rebuild/repair trigger, carrying truthful provenance.
- **SC1** — With `temporal-dev` stopped: the projection file exists and contains N active change summaries matching the on-disk per-change projection files, with truthful source.
- **SC3** — Projection regenerates correctly after a change mutation (create/archive/close) without a Temporal round-trip.

> Note: AC/SC inherited from the producer/consumer split agreed in `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` (toolbox). Not newly authored here; carried as cross-project contract provenance. Firming/clarification belongs to `/adv-discover`.

## Constraints

- Keep the CLI boundary intact — do NOT make `bin/adv` reach `plugin/src/storage` (`bin/lib/cli-source-boundary.test.ts`).
- Truthful provenance only — never emit `source:"temporal", live:true` for projection data (P33).
- Atomic write + versioned schema (reuse `atomicWriteFile`).
- Additive — do not break existing `adv status` / `adv epic list` consumers (they stay Temporal-live probes).
- Respect `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01` — terminal archive dominates; aggregate excludes archived/terminal changes.

## Related Repositories

- **toolbox** (`/home/jon/toolbox`) — consumer side: `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` reads `active-launcher-state.json` from zlauncher. The file-format contract (path, `schema_version`, provenance fields) is shared and must be coordinated.

## Discovery Findings

### Current State (verified in code)

- **Per-change disk projection ALREADY EXISTS** and is the aggregate writer's input source:
  - `plugin/src/temporal/activities.ts` → `writeChangeProjection` writes `{changeId}.json` (schemaVersion 2, full `ChangeWorkflowState`) into `projectionChangesDir`.
  - `projectionPath()` = `join(projectionChangesDir, ${changeId}.json)`.
  - Location: `projectionChangesDir` = `{externalRoot}/changes/` = `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/plugins/advance/{projectId}/changes/` (resolved via `getProjectPaths` in `plugin/src/storage/json.ts`, external root via `getExternalRoot` in `plugin/src/utils/project-id.ts`).
  - Written after EVERY mutating signal via `projectChangeState`/`scheduleChangeProjection` (`plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts:851-888`); `deleteActiveProjection` removes on terminal.
- **Atomic write primitive exists:** `atomicWriteFile` (`plugin/src/utils/fs.ts`) — temp + `fsync` + rename; also `writeJsonlAtomic` (`plugin/src/storage/jsonl-atomic-writer.ts`).
- **No aggregate/launcher projection exists** — `active-launcher-state` / `launcher-state` strings absent everywhere → genuinely new.
- **CLI boundary is explicit:** `bin/lib/live-status.ts` — "Default status must be live Temporal-backed for active rows. Disk projections may contribute terminal counts, but never active rows." Confirms the CLI stays Temporal-live; the launcher disk-projection is a separate consumer path.

### Spec Law

- `docs/specs/advance-workflow.md` → **`rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`** ("Durable Terminal Projection Dominates Stale Non-Terminal Shadows"): terminal archive dominates stale non-terminal workflow/memo/disk/visibility projections. The aggregate MUST exclude archived/terminal changes and respect archive-bundle dominance (cannot list a change as active if an archive bundle exists).

### Conflict Scan

- **No direct conflict.** No other change touches `active-launcher-state.json`.
- **Sibling epic members (`systemizeAdvOrchestration`):** `addDurableChangeSeeds` (order 13, execution — seeds change state durably; this change aggregates those seeds) and `improveCrossProject` (order 15, planning). Advisory order respected.
- **Related prior work (archived, durable-projection lineage):** `gateMutationSuccessDisk`, `fixDurableProofFallback`, `fixArchiveDurableProof` — inform the durability patterns this change reuses.
- **Pre-prep research packs:** no `*-prep.md` directly on this domain; `temp/brainstorm-adv-runtime-enhancements.md` and `temp/proposal-retireLegacyStorageBackend.md` are adjacent context (ADV runtime storage).

### Key Design Constraint

The aggregate writer is **host/activity-side, not a workflow responsibility**: aggregating requires reading ALL per-change `{changeId}.json` files, which is a cross-workflow read a single Temporal workflow cannot perform (a workflow owns only its own change state). Trigger: extend the existing `projectChangeState` post-signal hook to also regenerate the aggregate, plus a producer-owned MCP rebuild tool for drift recovery.

### LBP Check

Producer-owned aggregate read-projection is the validated long-term-best-practice direction (agreed in the parent `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal`). External-solution check: **skipped — purely internal architecture** (no external library/alternative viable; the constraint is the in-repo producer/consumer split + CLI boundary). No external alternatives evaluated.

### Open Design Questions

1. Freshness contract: eager regen after every mutation vs on-demand rebuild only (write amplification vs freshness guarantee).
2. Active-scope boundary: "active" = draft/non-terminal only, or also include recently-archived (recent history)?
3. Degraded-flag ownership: producer emits boolean `degraded` with threshold, or emits timestamp only and consumer classifies?

## Discovery Agenda (carried forward to design)

- Coordinate shared file-format contract with `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` (toolbox): `schema_version`, field names, provenance semantics. (Toolbox target worker not serviceable at discovery time — coordinate at design/implementation.)
- Worktree-branch data gap: per-change `ChangeWorkflowState` lacks registered worktree paths — derive `change/<id>` convention or add a projection field.
- Active-summary cap value (match launcher display; consumer-determined).

## Root Cause Analysis (defect-origin, inherited)

**Defect origin:** zlauncher's ADV display silently vanished on Temporal outage.

**Evidence gathered:**
- Tier 1 (local, advance): the standalone `adv status` / `adv epic list` CLI is Temporal-hard with no disk-fallback (`bin/lib/live-status.ts`); the MCP `adv_change_list` layer has disk-fallback; per-change `change.json`/`{changeId}.json` durability exists via `persistStateToDiskDurable`/`writeChangeProjection`.
- Tier 2 (external, toolbox): consumer-side RCA in `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` confirmed the launcher read path lacked the disk-fallback.

**Leading hypothesis:** the read path lacks a producer-owned durable aggregate projection; the validated fix is to produce one rather than patch the intentionally storage-free CLI boundary.

**Ruled-out paths:** patching the CLI to gain a disk-fallback (rejected — violates `bin/lib/cli-source-boundary.test.ts` and the Bun-safe/storage-free CLI design).

**Spec-law impact:** introduces an aggregate-projection obligation consistent with `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`; a new `rq-*` for launcher read-projection provenance truthfulness is likely warranted (design phase).

—

**Bypass rationale:** RCA produced inline (inherited from the cross-project parent change `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal`) rather than via a fresh `/adv-problem` run, because the producer/consumer split and defect origin were already established in the parent agreement.

# Design — Add ADV Launcher Read Projection

## Architecture Overview

Producer-owned aggregate read-projection. Two layers:

1. **Pure aggregator** (`plugin/src/storage/launcher-projection.ts`, NEW) — reads all `{changeId}.json` per-change projections from `{externalRoot}/changes/`, filters to active (non-terminal, no archive bundle), derives bounded summaries, computes truthful provenance, returns an in-memory `LauncherProjection`. Pure function: no ADV/Temporal calls; fully testable in isolation.

2. **Writer + lifecycle** (`plugin/src/temporal/activities.ts`) — the EXISTING `writeChangeProjection` activity body is extended to also write `active-launcher-state.json` (aggregate) at `{externalRoot}/`, in the same host-side execution that already writes the per-change projection. No new activity is added to the workflow. Plus a producer-owned MCP rebuild tool for drift recovery.

**Why host-side, not a workflow:** aggregation reads ALL change projection files — a cross-workflow read. A Temporal workflow is sandboxed and owns only its own change state; it cannot enumerate sibling workflows' files. Activities run on the host worker and can read the filesystem broadly. So the aggregate lives in the activity/host layer.

**Why extend the existing activity body, not add a new activity call (replay-safety):** adding a new `await activity()` to a workflow handler changes the recorded activity sequence → in-flight workflow histories break on replay (`NonDeterminismError`) and would require `wf.patch`/Worker versioning + replay tests. Extending the body of the ALREADY-CALLED `writeChangeProjection` activity is replay-safe: Temporal records the activity *invocation* (name + args), not the body; activity bodies are host-side and freely extensible. The workflow still calls the same activity with the same args, so existing histories replay identically.

**Data flow (replay-safe — workflow code unchanged):**
```
mutating signal
  → workflow state updated
  → projectChangeState()                       [workflows.ts:851]
      → writeChangeProjection({projectionChangesDir, state, projectedAt})   (existing invocation)
          [activity body, host-side]
          → write changes/{changeId}.json              (per-change, existing)
          → buildLauncherProjection({changesDir, archiveDir, generatedAt, threshold})  (NEW, pure)
          → atomicWriteFile active-launcher-state.json (aggregate, NEW)
```

The activity derives `externalRoot = dirname(projectionChangesDir)` and `archiveDir = join(externalRoot, "archive")` from its existing `projectionChangesDir` arg — no signature change, no workflow change.

## Key Decisions

### KD-1 — Extend the existing `writeChangeProjection` activity body (replay-safe); do NOT add a new activity to the workflow
Cross-workflow read requires host-side execution; the existing activity is already the host-side surface invoked on every mutation. Extending its body (rather than adding a new `await activity()` to the workflow) preserves workflow-history determinism for in-flight workflows. Validated against the Temporal TypeScript determinism model (AGENTS.md: the SDK sandbox patches `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in *workflow* code; *activities* are host-side, unpatched, and not part of the replayed workflow history — only their invocation is recorded).

### KD-2 — Reuse `atomicWriteFile` (utils/fs.ts)
Same primitive the per-change projection uses (temp + fsync + rename). Concurrent multi-session writers to the same aggregate converge: `atomicWriteFile` guarantees last-writer-wins with no torn file; content is deterministic (sorted) so concurrent writes produce equivalent files.

### KD-3 — Eager regeneration (user decision)
Aggregate regenerates after every mutation, inside the same activity that writes the per-change projection. Cost: one extra `read-N + write-1` filesystem op per signal. Accepted (user chose guaranteed-fresh over write-churn reduction).

### KD-4 — Active filter: `status==="draft"` AND no archive bundle, matched by canonical `change.json.id`
Spec-law compliant (`rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`). Two conditions:
- `state.status === "draft"` read from the per-change projection
- no archive bundle whose canonical `change.json.id` equals the changeId (terminal truth dominates stale non-terminal shadows)

Per the spec's dedupe rule (`docs/specs/advance-workflow.md` rq-terminalProjectionTruth01): archive bundles MUST be deduped/matched by the canonical `change.json.id` inside the bundle, **not** by archive directory name. The aggregator reads each archive bundle's `change.json` and matches `.id`; this defends against stale `{changeId}.json` left by a wedged/terminal workflow that never ran `deleteActiveProjection`, and against archive directories whose names diverge from the canonical id.

### KD-5 — Degraded = timestamp + advisory flag (user decision)
- `freshness` = max `lastSignalAt` across active summaries (ISO timestamp)
- `degraded` = advisory boolean, `now - freshness > DEGRADED_THRESHOLD_MS`
- `generated_at` = host write time
- `degraded` / `generated_at` use host `Date.now()` — legal because the aggregator runs in the activity/host context, NOT workflow code (workflow code must be deterministic; host activities are unpatched and not replayed). Validator confirmed host-side Activity I/O and host `Date.now()` are sound.

### KD-6 — epics_available:false (truthful)
Active epics remain Temporal-only. The aggregate NEVER fabricates epic data as live. Consumers needing epic data must use Temporal. Hard truthful-provenance constraint (P33).

### KD-7 — Rebuild trigger = MCP tool, not a `bin/adv` subcommand
CLI source-boundary guard (`bin/lib/cli-source-boundary.test.ts`) forbids `bin/adv` reaching `plugin/src/storage`. The rebuild trigger is a producer-owned MCP tool (`adv_launcher_projection_rebuild`) registered in `tool-registry.ts`, calling the same pure aggregator.

### KD-8 — schema_version:1, wrapper-first
Mirror the per-change projection's wrapper-first convention (`schemaVersion: 2`). Aggregate uses `schema_version: 1` (snake_case to match the cross-project consumer contract convention; coordinated with toolbox `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal`).

## ADR Drafts

### ADR 0009 (DRAFT, advisory) — Launcher aggregate projection is host/activity-side; written by extending the existing projection activity body

**Status:** Draft (advisory; does not gate-block)
**Rubric:** hard-to-reverse (✓ wired into the activity body + consumer contract) + surprising-without-context (✓ "why not a workflow query / why not a new activity?") + result-of-real-tradeoff (✓ replay-safety constrains the mechanism).

**Context:** The launcher needs a single file aggregating all active changes. Two natural-looking options exist: a Temporal workflow query, or a new activity invoked from the workflow.

**Decision:** The aggregate is written by extending the body of the EXISTING `writeChangeProjection` activity (host-side), invoked on every mutation. It is neither a workflow query nor a newly-added workflow activity call.

**Rationale:** (1) a workflow query is impossible — aggregation is a cross-workflow read and workflows are sandboxed to their own state; (2) adding a new `await activity()` to the workflow breaks replay determinism for in-flight histories; (3) extending an already-invoked activity's body is replay-safe because only the invocation (name+args), not the body, is recorded in workflow history.

**Consequences:** Aggregate regen is host filesystem I/O with no Temporal availability dependency (the whole point). Zero workflow-code change → zero migration/versioning burden. Multi-session convergence via atomic write. (Full ADR `docs/adr/0009-launcher-projection-host-side.md` written at execution.)

## Implementation Strategy

1. `plugin/src/storage/launcher-projection.ts` (NEW) — pure aggregator + Zod schema (`LauncherProjectionSchema`, `LauncherChangeSummarySchema`). Exports `buildLauncherProjection({ changesDir, archiveDir, generatedAt, degradedThresholdMs })`.
2. `plugin/src/storage/launcher-projection.test.ts` (NEW) — unit tests (filtering, archive-bundle exclusion by canonical id, freshness/degraded, empty state, sorting, cap).
3. `plugin/src/temporal/activities.ts` — extend `writeChangeProjection` body: after writing `{changeId}.json`, derive `externalRoot`/`archiveDir`, call `buildLauncherProjection`, `atomicWriteFile` the aggregate. Mirror the existing error handling (best-effort: aggregate failure must NOT fail the per-change projection write).
4. `plugin/src/tools/launcher-projection.ts` (NEW) — MCP rebuild tool + register in `plugin/src/tool-registry.ts`.
5. Integration test — signal-driven regeneration with Temporal stopped (covers SC1/SC3); replay-safety check that an in-flight workflow history with the original activity call still replays (the activity body extension is transparent to replay).
6. Cross-project contract coordination with `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` (toolbox): confirm `schema_version` / field names.

Sequencing: aggregator + schema (pure, testable) → extend activity body → MCP tool → integration + replay tests.

## LBP Analysis

Producer-owned aggregate read-projection is the validated long-term approach (agreed in parent `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal`). Alternatives considered:

- **Workflow query** — impossible (cross-workflow read). Rejected (KD-1).
- **New activity added to the workflow** — breaks replay determinism for in-flight histories; requires versioning + replay tests. Rejected in favor of KD-1 (extend existing activity body).
- **Patch the CLI for a disk-fallback** — violates CLI boundary + Bun-safe/storage-free design. Rejected (DONT1).
- **Per-change consumer reads each `{changeId}.json`** — shifts aggregation to every consumer (N reads per consumer vs 1 aggregate). Rejected (parent agreement chose producer-owned aggregate).
- **CQRS-lite: separate projection worker process** — over-engineering; reuses the existing activity path with no new process. Rejected.

## Affected Components

- `plugin/src/storage/launcher-projection.ts` (NEW) — pure aggregator + schema
- `plugin/src/temporal/activities.ts` — extend `writeChangeProjection` body (no signature/workflow change)
- `plugin/src/tools/launcher-projection.ts` (NEW) — MCP rebuild tool
- `plugin/src/tool-registry.ts` — register rebuild tool
- `plugin/src/utils/fs.ts` — reuse `atomicWriteFile` (no change)
- `plugin/src/utils/project-id.ts` — reuse `getExternalRoot` (no change)
- `docs/specs/advance-workflow.md` — new `rq-*` for launcher-projection provenance truthfulness (spec delta at planning)
- Cross-project: `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` (toolbox) — shared file-format contract

## Design-Derived Criteria (technical, architecture-caused — not new user-facing AC)

- **DDC1 (performance budget):** aggregate regen < 50ms for typical N≤50 active changes (read N small JSONs + write 1). Scales linearly with active count.
- **DDC2 (degraded threshold):** default `DEGRADED_THRESHOLD_MS = 300_000` (5 min). Documented; consumer-overridable via its own classification of `freshness`.
- **DDC3 (atomicity):** reuse `atomicWriteFile`; concurrent readers observe old-or-new, never torn (SC4).
- **DDC4 (summary cap):** active summaries bounded to 50, sorted by `last_activity` desc; consumer truncates display. Producer must not under-bound the launcher's view.
- **DDC5 (host-time legality):** `degraded` / `generated_at` use host `Date.now()` — permitted because the aggregator runs in activity/host context, not the workflow sandbox (validator confirmed).
- **DDC6 (replay-safety):** zero workflow-code change; the activity invocation sequence is unchanged, so in-flight workflow histories replay identically. No `wf.patch`/versioning required.

## Design Leverage Scout

Scout: performed inline — the reuse surface was comprehensively mapped during discovery and is fully integrated into the design (writeChangeProjection, atomicWriteFile, getExternalRoot, ChangeWorkflowState). Candidates considered:

1. **Reuse `writeChangeProjection` activity (extend body) wholesale** — auto-adopted (KD-1, KD-2). The aggregate write piggybacks the existing host-side execution; no new activity or workflow change.
2. **Share summary schema with existing archive-summary renderer** — surfaced (not auto-adopted): `tools/archive-summary.renderBriefSummary` already derives change summaries; a shared summary type could reduce duplication. Risk: couples the producer contract to an internal renderer. → Defer to planning: assess whether the launcher summary shape and archive-summary shape can share a type without coupling the cross-project contract. Low risk if shapes differ.
3. **Rebuild tool could also serve conformance CI** — surfaced: a conformance check could read `active-launcher-state.json` for offline active-set validation. Out of scope for this change (conformance is a consumer); noted as a future consumer, not built here.

Auto-adopted: 1 (KD-1/KD-2). Surfaced to planning: 2. Noted as future: 3.

## Risks / Mitigations

- **Workflow replay determinism (validator blocker, resolved)** — resolved by KD-1/DDC6: extend the existing activity body, not the workflow's activity-call sequence. No versioning/replay-test burden beyond confirming transparency.
- **Archive dedupe by directory name (validator blocker, resolved)** — resolved by KD-4: match canonical `change.json.id` inside archive bundles, per `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`.
- **Write amplification under signal bursts** — accepted (user chose eager). Mitigation: cheap for N≤50; host-side (no Temporal load). Debounce is the deferred fallback if it becomes a problem.
- **Multi-session concurrent writes** — `atomicWriteFile` last-writer-wins + deterministic sorted content → convergence, no corruption.
- **Aggregate failure must not break per-change projection** — the activity writes the per-change projection first; the aggregate write is best-effort and logs on failure (mirrors existing `projectChangeState` warn-on-failure pattern).
- **Shared-contract drift with toolbox** — mitigation: coordinate `schema_version` / field names with `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal` at implementation; document the contract.
- **`degraded` threshold misclassification** — advisory flag only; consumer may override using the raw `freshness` timestamp.

## Validator Result

**validation.status: fail (advisory-only — resolved in-design)** — Phase 3.5 independent adv-researcher validation. (Note: the researcher's durable report submission was rejected by the active transport schema; findings are authoritative and recorded here.)

Two in-scope blockers raised, both resolved by design revision above:

1. **Workflow determinism** — adding a new awaited activity to the workflow needs Temporal patch/versioning + replay tests for existing histories (cited Temporal TS workflow-versioning docs; `workflows.ts:851-876`).
   → **Resolved:** KD-1/DDC6 — extend the existing `writeChangeProjection` activity body; the activity *invocation* (what the workflow records) is unchanged, so replay is safe and no versioning is required.
2. **Archive suppression must match canonical `change.json.id`, not directory names** (cited `docs/specs/advance-workflow.md` rq-terminalProjectionTruth01, `json.ts`).
   → **Resolved:** KD-4 — aggregator reads each archive bundle's `change.json` and matches by canonical `.id`.

Validator confirmed SOUND: host-side Activity I/O, host `Date.now()`, and `atomicWriteFile`.

No contract compromise, no security/release blocker, no user-discovered CONFLICT. The approved AC/SC are unchanged; the revisions only refine HOW AC2/AC3 are delivered (sounder mechanism). Advisory `fail` does not gate-block; blockers resolved in-design.

# Executive Summary — Add ADV Launcher Read Projection

## Outcome

ADV now produces a durable, launcher-consumable aggregate read-projection (`active-launcher-state.json`) so that active changes remain visible to the launcher (and any file-reading consumer) even when Temporal — ADV's system of record — is unavailable. This is the **producer side** of a producer/consumer split with the toolbox change `decoupleAdvDisplayTemporal`, which made `zellij-project-launcher` read this file instead of shelling out to a Temporal-hard CLI.

## Why It Matters

Previously, the launcher silently vanished on any Temporal outage: the standalone `adv status` / `adv epic list` CLI is Temporal-hard with no disk fallback, while agents kept working via the MCP layer. Users lost visibility into active work precisely when infrastructure was degraded. This change makes the launcher display Temporal-independent for active changes — it reads a single, stable, versioned file rather than probing a live service.

## What Was Built

- A **pure aggregator** (`plugin/src/storage/launcher-projection.ts`) that combines the existing per-change `{changeId}.json` projections into one bounded, truthful-provenance summary (draft/non-terminal only, terminal-truth-compliant, capped at 50, freshness + advisory `degraded` flag, `epics_available:false`).
- The **existing `writeChangeProjection` activity body** was extended (host-side) to atomically write the aggregate alongside the per-change projection — with **no new workflow activity call**, so in-flight workflow histories replay identically (no versioning/migration needed).
- A producer-owned **MCP rebuild tool** (`adv_launcher_projection_rebuild`) for drift recovery — plugin-only, never reachable from the Bun-safe `bin/adv` CLI.
- A new spec law (`rq-launcherProjectionTruth01`) and **ADR 0009** codifying the host-side, replay-safe design.

## Verification

- 12 aggregator unit tests, 7 activity tests, 1 Temporal integration test (signal-driven regeneration with Temporal stopped), and 1 replay-safety guard test — all green; typecheck/lint clean; CLI source boundary green.
- Independent design validation (adv-researcher) and an independent acceptance review (adv-reviewer) both run; the one design blocker (workflow replay determinism) and the one acceptance blocker (refresh granularity) were resolved in-design/in-criteria.
- Contract review matrix: 19/19 items passing.

## Key Decision

The aggregate is written **host-side by extending an existing activity's body**, not by adding a new activity to the workflow. A workflow-level change would have broken replay determinism for every in-flight change; extending an already-invoked activity is replay-safe. This keeps the change low-risk and migration-free.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- **Projection refresh granularity:** the projection refreshes at gate transitions and terminal mutations (create/archive/close) — the existing projection system's trigger points — plus on-demand via the rebuild tool. It does not refresh on every within-gate task/artifact mutation. Acceptance criteria were re-scoped (user-approved) to match this rather than risk a workflow-replay-breaking change. A future host-side per-mutation trigger could tighten freshness.
- **Cross-project consumer path (IMPORTANT):** the shipped toolbox consumer reads the projection from `…/advance/external/{projectId}/`, but this producer writes the canonical `…/advance/{projectId}/` (no `external/`). The producer path is correct (consistent with all other advance external state); the consumer has a path bug (it was tested only against fixtures). A toolbox follow-up to drop the `external/` segment was approved; its creation is blocked until the toolbox ADV worker is serviceable. **End-to-end producer→consumer will not connect until that consumer fix lands.** Recorded durably.
- Active-epic offline projection remains out of scope (epics stay Temporal-only; `epics_available:false` is truthful).

## Release Readiness

Producer change is complete, tested, and spec-law-backed. The one open dependency is the cross-project consumer path fix (separate repo, separate shipped change), which does not block archiving this producer change but does block end-to-end launcher functionality until resolved.
